principle: Full-stack software, built by chat. Shipped from your pocket.
intro: Morpheus turns a phone into a complete software studio. Describe what you want in plain language; Morpheus writes the real code, builds the backend, compiles a native binary, and deploys it — no laptop, no lock-in, no illusions. You own every file. Beside it, in the same account, sits Jarvis: a personal assistant with his own long-term memory, a Command Deck for the rest of your life, and a dock you can put on a website you already run. Both are being built toward a digital possibility engine — everything you tell them, brought together, so it can surface opportunities and possibilities you had not seen.
closing: Morpheus is not a no-code toy. It's a real dev team in your pocket — one that ships standalone, deployable software you fully own.

possibility.title: A digital possibility engine
possibility.body: The destination rather than a shipped feature — and the reason Jarvis exists. Everything you tell Morpheus and Jarvis is kept, brought together, and read back so it can surface opportunities and possibilities you had not seen. Jarvis's suggestions is the first working piece of it: he reads across your own Command Deck unprompted and tells you what you may have missed, and switching that widget off stops it dead with no AI spend.

audio.title: Audio — your amp, in the box
audio.intro: Morpheus builds real audio plugins around a neural amp model. Put a .nam model in the project, add a cabinet impulse response if you have one, pick the target for your machine and COMPILE — the build runs on a hosted runner, and the finished plugin lands in _compiled/ with a proof file the build itself wrote. The model is played by NeuralAmpModelerCore, the reference implementation of the format, and the signal path around it is a measured design rather than a sketch: input trim, gate, bass/mid/treble, the neural model, the cabinet, output.
audio.routesIntro: A plugin format exists on more than one platform, so a target that named only its formats would read as "builds for whatever you are on". Each route below is one machine and says so; a plugin compiled for the wrong one loads nowhere and explains nothing.

routes.formats: VST3, Audio Unit, CLAP, and a standalone app
routes.detail: The only route that can produce an Audio Unit, because there is no AU outside Apple's platforms.

routes.formats: VST3, CLAP, and a standalone app
routes.detail: No Audio Unit, and that is not an omission — it is what Windows hosts load.

routes.runsOn: 64-bit ARM Linux only (a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5, for instance)
routes.formats: VST3, CLAP, and a standalone app
routes.detail: A 64-bit ARM ELF, which is what a Raspberry Pi runs — not an x86 Linux binary.

steps.detail: A .nam file — train your own, or download one. Put it in the project: models/amp.nam is what the builder looks for first, and the compile panel tells you which file it found, or says there is none.

Optional, but it matters: a modelled amp on its own sounds like a bee in a jar. Upload a cabinet impulse response as a .wav in the CABINET dialog and it is baked into the plugin — nothing to install beside it. Only the first 4096 samples are convolved, so a 48 kHz IR of roughly 85 ms is the whole of it.
audio-plugin-macos, audio-plugin-windows or audio-plugin-linux-arm — whichever one you will actually open it on. They are not interchangeable.

COMPILE pushes the project to your own GitHub and runs the build there. When it finishes the plugin is in _compiled/ with BUILD-PROOF.txt beside it. Unzip, and put the VST3, AU or CLAP in your plugin folder; the standalone needs no installation at all.

Six controls, all of them in your host's automation list: Input (±24 dB), Gate (off to 0 dB), Bass, Mid and Treble (±12 dB each) and Output. The gate's bottom position is OFF rather than a very low threshold, so it is exactly transparent when you do not want it.

audio.measured: The proof is a measurement the build makes and writes down, not a claim. The plugin's own entry point and NeuralAmpModelerCore's own renderer were given the same dry signal from the same pinned commit and compared sample by sample: they agree to −144.0 dB on a 64-bit ARM runner. The chain around it was measured the same way — bass, mid and treble each inside 0.5 dB of the filter that designed them, the cabinet nulling to −147.5 dB against a direct convolution of its own impulse response, and the gate taking the quiet part 44.8 dB below the loud one.

planned.status: built and measured, in the repository rather than in the app
planned.detail: The awkward part of capturing an amp is not the recording, it is knowing whether the recording can be trained on. Morpheus can now fetch the re-amp signal the trainer accepts, check a recorded pair against the trainer's own rules before anyone spends an hour of GPU time — sample rate, length, whether the amp held still for the whole take, the delay it will be aligned at — and then measure the model that comes back against the recording. Today that is a command-line tool in the repository, not a panel in the app.

planned.what: A Raspberry Pi you plug in and play
planned.detail: The plugin above runs on a Pi. A bootable image that carries the plugin, the audio routing and the first-boot setup, controlled from your phone, is the next step — the image target exists, it is the audio host that does not yet.

planned.what: A practice amp with no operating system
planned.detail: The same model in a small microcontroller, for the cheapest and most deterministic tier: no OS, no buffering, fixed latency.

planned.what: Effects pedals and instruments that are programmable logic
planned.detail: Running quantized models on an FPGA. The open question is not whether a network fits — it is what low bit-widths cost the sound, and that gets measured before anything is bought.

downloads.title: Downloads
downloads.intro: Everything Morpheus hands you as a file, in one place. Most of what you make is deliberately not here: your builds land in your own project, in your own repository, in _compiled/ — which is the point.

items.name: Portable Morpheus
items.what: The whole product — the builder and the Command Deck — running on your own machine. Your data stays with you, and nothing stops working if you stop paying.
items.note: A ZIP of the product's own source, generated at build time from the repository. Published source, not open source — see the notice inside.

items.name: The user manual
items.what: How to install and run what Morpheus builds, for every target it builds — including what each platform's unsigned-software warning means, and how to get past it.
items.note: Generated at build time from the same module that writes USER-MANUAL.txt into every build, so the published manual cannot drift from the one a download carries.

items.name: Audio plugin — demo builds
items.platform: Windows · Linux AArch64 · macOS on request
items.what: A prebuilt plugin you can load in a DAW today: a neural amp model from NeuralAmpModelerCore with an input trim, a noise gate and a three-band tone stack, in VST3, CLAP and a standalone app.
items.note: Unsigned, so your platform will warn once. This is the amplifier stage and not the product — what Morpheus makes for you is a plugin built in your own repository around your own model and your own cabinet.

items.name: Marketplace templates
items.what: Working projects other people have published — buy one or install it into your workspace in a tap, and read every file before you run it.
items.note: Published by other users, not by us. Sellers get a cut.

downloads.ownHeading: What you compile is not a download from us
downloads.own: Every target compiles inside your own GitHub repository and its output lands in _compiled/ in your own project: an Android APK, an iOS app, a macOS app, a Windows EXE, a Linux binary, a Raspberry Pi image, a full Linux distro, a Python package, a web app, or a VST3 / Audio Unit / CLAP plugin. That is the difference between a download page and a build tool — the file is yours, in your account, from your source.

capabilities.title: Chat-to-code
capabilities.body: Describe an app in a sentence; Morpheus writes production-ready frontend and backend code you can read, edit, and own. No pseudo-code, no placeholders.
capabilities.workflow: Type your request in the chat bar → Morpheus plans the file structure → writes each file in full → runs a review pass → saves to the file tree. Tap REVERT beneath your message to undo that prompt.

capabilities.title: Autonomous build pipeline
capabilities.body: A self-correcting loop: compile → run → on failure, an AI agent reads the logs, writes a fix, and recompiles — only escalating to you when it's truly stuck.
capabilities.workflow: Tap the bot icon in the chat bar → describe the full scope → watch the multi-step log in real time → STOP anytime. On a failed step it reads the error logs, writes a fix, and recompiles automatically.

capabilities.title: One chat, every target
capabilities.body: Compile the same project to a web app, Windows EXE, macOS app, Linux binary, Android APK, iOS app, Python package, or Arduino firmware — all from your phone.
capabilities.workflow: Pick a compile target in the toolbar → tap COMPILE → Morpheus pushes a GitHub Actions workflow → the build runs on a hosted runner → the artifact lands in _compiled/ ready to download.

capabilities.title: Audio plugins — a modelled amp, compiled for your machine
capabilities.body: Compile a real VST3, Audio Unit or CLAP plugin around a neural amp model and a cabinet impulse response, for macOS, Windows or 64-bit ARM Linux. The model is baked into the binary and played by the reference implementation of the format, so there is nothing to install beside it. The signal path — input trim, gate, three-band tone, the model, the cabinet — is measured against a reference on every build, and the build writes what it verified into your download.
capabilities.workflow: Open a project → put your .nam in the file tree (models/ is searched first) → CABINET dialog to add a speaker impulse response if you have one → set the target to audio-plugin-macos, audio-plugin-windows or audio-plugin-linux-arm → COMPILE → unzip _compiled/ and load the plugin in your DAW. BUILD-PROOF.txt beside it is the build's own record of what it checked.

capabilities.title: Bootable OS images
capabilities.body: Bake your app into a Raspberry Pi image or a full PC/server Linux distro (Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora) that boots and runs your software on first start. Customise hostname, timezone, locale, SSH, and packages at build time.
capabilities.workflow: Open Distro Config → set hostname, timezone, locale, SSH keys, packages → COMPILE → flash the .img to an SD card with flash.sh, or push it to a remote device with flash-network.sh over SSH.

capabilities.title: Auto-generated backends
capabilities.body: Morpheus plans, writes, and deploys a backend (API, database, auth) for your app, then wires the frontend to it automatically.
capabilities.workflow: Open the Architect → describe the API → Morpheus plans the schema and routes → generates the server code → deploy to a connected host → use Wire to Backend to point the frontend at the live URL.

capabilities.title: Marketplace
capabilities.body: Publish your project as a paid template; browse, buy, and install others' templates in one tap. Sellers get a cut, buyers get working code.
capabilities.workflow: Finish a project → Marketplace panel → Publish tab → add icon, screenshots, description, price (min $0.50) → Publish. Buyers tap BUY → Stripe checkout → download the ZIP, or tap INSTALL to copy it into their workspace.

capabilities.title: Network flashing
capabilities.body: Push a finished OS image straight to a Pi or server over SSH — no SD-card swapping, no disk juggling.

capabilities.title: GitHub, end-to-end
capabilities.body: OAuth in, import existing repos, push new code, and trigger remote builds via GitHub Actions — your code lives in your own account.

capabilities.title: Live deploy with log-pulling
capabilities.body: Connect Cloudflare, Vercel, Supabase and others; Morpheus deploys and then pulls live logs back so you can watch it run.

capabilities.title: AI diagnosis
capabilities.body: When a build or deploy breaks, an AI agent analyses the real error logs and either auto-fixes or hands you a precise, actionable next step.

capabilities.title: Dependency sync
capabilities.body: One tap updates every dependency across npm, pip, Maven, Cargo, Go, Gem, Composer, Gradle, and PlatformIO — nested manifests included.

capabilities.title: Cost transparency
capabilities.body: Every AI action shows its estimated compute cost in USD up front, so you always know what you're spending.

capabilities.title: Perpetual project memory
capabilities.body: Every message you type and every file Morpheus writes is stored permanently with the construct. On each build, the full conversation history and the complete file tree are fed back in as context — so Morpheus never forgets a requirement, a decision, or a fix from earlier in the project. The more you tell him, the better he builds.
capabilities.workflow: Just chat normally — every prompt is saved to the construct's permanent record. When you ask for the next change, Morpheus re-reads the entire history and all current files before building, so earlier decisions carry forward automatically.

capabilities.title: Searchable project history
capabilities.body: An important diagnostics tool. Every chat message, build log, tool action, diagnosis, and file snapshot is stored permanently and searchable end-to-end. When something breaks or a requirement drifts, search the full record to find exactly when, why, and what changed — no scrolling, no guessing.
capabilities.workflow: Open the History panel → BUILD LOGS to search event details and tool names; SNAPSHOTS to find a saved state by label; CHAT to search every message Morpheus has ever written for this construct. Each tab shows a live match count and highlights results in context.

capabilities.title: Help mode
capabilities.body: Toggle it on and tap any feature; Morpheus explains what it does and how to use it, inline.

capabilities.title: Voice
capabilities.body: On demand, Morpheus speaks its replies aloud — for hands-free building on the go.

capabilities.title: Jarvis — the personal assistant
capabilities.body: Morpheus is the builder; Jarvis is the assistant — a second product in the same account, at /deck, with his own connections, his own long-term memory and his own chat history rather than a view onto Morpheus's. You talk or dictate freely and Jarvis splits what you said into separate thoughts, files each one where it belongs — a task, a strategy note, something worth keeping, or one of the five life streams (health, money, home, people, growth) — assigns the owner, and keeps your original words instead of replacing them with a summary. Ask him for a synthesis and he reasons across everything he has been told; turn on Voice and he reads the reply aloud as it is being written.
capabilities.workflow: Open /deck → type or dictate into Brain dump, the capture box pinned to the top of the page → Jarvis separates the thoughts, assigns each to the right stream and the right person, and remembers all of it. Ask him anything in the Jarvis tab — every message is kept in his permanent history and read back to him as context.

capabilities.title: Command Deck — a dashboard for your own life
capabilities.body: Jarvis's home: a configurable dashboard at /deck with 15 widgets — the five life streams (health, money, home, people, growth), a task board, an inbox, a calendar, strategy, a signal chain and a knowledge base, with the brain-dump capture box pinned first and a permanent record behind every one. Each account sees only its own Deck, and which widgets appear, and in what order, is per account.
capabilities.workflow: Open /deck → Deck Settings → Widgets to switch widgets on or off and reorder them. Jarvis's suggestions is also the per-account opt-out from proactive insight: switch it off and he stops reading across your Deck unprompted, and no AI credit is spent on it.

capabilities.title: Morpheus Dock — the plugin for a site you already run
capabilities.body: Put Morpheus on your own website. Mint a scoped widget token, paste one script tag, and the site gets the dock: the same chat, deploy, site-health, shop, pages, SEO and traffic panels, floating over your own pages. It renders inside a shadow root, so the host site's CSS cannot bleed in or out, and it passes the page you are looking at into the chat so answers can be grounded in what is on screen. The Morpheus WordPress plugin ships the same dock and also carries Morpheus's deploys onto the live site, signed with an HMAC the plugin verifies.
capabilities.workflow: Project → WEBSITE panel → EMBED tab → create a token, ticking the scopes you want (chat, deploy, store, SEO, traffic; the secret is shown once and only its hash is stored) → copy the script tag onto the site, or use one-tap dock setup to push it to a connected WordPress site. The floating corner dock comes from data-dock="1"; without it the panel drops inline where the tag sits. Revoke a token at any time from the same list.

examples.title: Build a Task Tracker from Scratch
examples.scenario: From an empty workspace to a running web app in four messages. This is the most common path: you describe, Morpheus writes, you refine, you export.

steps.note: Tap NEW CONSTRUCT, give it a name, and pick a compile target.
Type your request in plain English. Morpheus plans the files, writes them, and runs a review pass.
lines: > Build a task tracker. Add a task, mark it done, delete it. Clean modern UI.
M: Review pass: no issues found.
[OK] 4 files saved to the file tree

steps.note: The preview panel builds automatically and renders your app live.
lines: M: Your app is running in the preview panel.
M: Try adding a task — it updates instantly.

steps.note: Ask for changes in chat; each prompt only touches the files it needs. Tap REVERT under a message to undo it. ZIP downloads the whole project.
lines: > Make the Add button green and larger.
M: Updated TaskForm.jsx — button now bg-green, h-12.

examples.title: Compile to an Android APK
examples.scenario: Turn the same project into an installable Android app. Morpheus pushes your code to GitHub, triggers a build on a hosted runner, and drops the APK into your project.

steps.note: Change the compile target in the toolbar to android apk.
Tap COMPILE. Morpheus creates a repo, pushes your code, and runs a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the APK.

steps.action: If the build fails, it self-heals
steps.note: When a step fails, the AI diagnosis agent reads the logs, writes a fix, and recompiles — only asking you if it's truly stuck.
lines: M: Found a missing resource in AndroidManifest.xml.

steps.note: The finished artifact lands in _compiled/ inside your project, ready to download to your phone.
lines: M: Tap the APK to download it to your phone and install.

examples.title: Publish to the Marketplace
examples.scenario: Sell a finished project as a template. You set the listing; Morpheus creates a Stripe price; buyers pay and install in one tap.

steps.note: With a finished project open, tap EARN in the toolbar.
Upload an icon, write a description, and set a price (minimum $0.50 to meet Stripe checkout rules).
lines: > Description: A clean task tracker with add/complete/delete.

steps.note: Morpheus creates a Stripe price and lists your template on the public Market.
Buyers tap BUY, pay via Stripe, then either download a ZIP or INSTALL the template straight into their workspace.
lines: [OK] Installed — buyer now owns the code.

examples.title: Bake a Raspberry Pi Image
examples.scenario: Bake your app into a bootable Raspberry Pi OS image that runs your software on first boot. Configure once, compile, then flash an SD card.

steps.note: Set the rpi-distro target, then open Distro Config to set hostname, timezone, locale, SSH keys, and packages.
Morpheus clones pi-gen, injects your app, and builds the image. This takes roughly 20 minutes.
The build ships flash.sh and a README. Write the image to an SD card, or push it to a remote Pi over SSH with flash-network.sh.
lines: [OK] Done. Boot your Pi — the app starts on first login.
